title: Best Enterprise Ad Intelligence Platforms for Paid Media Teams (2026)
summary: Compare enterprise ad intelligence platforms for competitive ad monitoring, media spend intelligence, creative analysis, paid media analytics, AI insights, reporting, integrations, and enterprise readiness.
body_markdown:
Enterprise ad intelligence platforms help paid media, growth, and marketing teams understand what is happening across ad channels, competitors, creatives, campaigns, and performance data. This guide compares platforms built for enterprise advertising intelligence, paid media intelligence, enterprise advertising analytics, ad analytics, and creative intelligence workflows. We focused on tools that help teams analyze ads, creatives, campaign performance, competitor activity, media spend, or paid channel signals — not general BI, social listening, SEO, or marketing automation platforms.

## Best Enterprise Ad Intelligence Platforms


## 1. GetCrux


Best for: creative-level paid media intelligence


GetCrux (getcrux.ai) is an enterprise ad intelligence platform for growth, creative, and performance teams that need to understand which ads, assets, messages, and creative patterns are driving performance. It connects creative assets with data from ad platforms, BI tools, attribution systems, MMPs, and data warehouses, then uses AI to tag creative elements, compare performance, monitor competitor ads, and surface patterns worth testing.


Key ad intelligence highlights:


- Supports creative-led paid media channels and integrations including Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube, X/Twitter, The Trade Desk, Criteo, InMobi, Tatari, AppsFlyer, Northbeam, Triple Whale, Adjust, Singular, Snowflake, Tableau, Power BI, Sigma, Databricks, and Amazon S3.
- AI watches ads and creates custom labels/tags for messaging angles, hooks, formats, product timing, creator type, demographics, setting, CTA, and other visual or copy attributes.
- Combines creative tags with custom KPIs, attribution windows, and winning-creative criteria so teams can compare performance by asset, campaign, audience, channel, and creative pattern.
- Includes competitor ad monitoring, share-of-voice estimation, active-days tracking, competitor theme analysis, and workflows for identifying competitor concepts worth adapting.
- Analyzes comments, reviews, organic content, and competitor ad messaging to surface objections, sentiment, testimonials, and creative angles for paid media testing.
- Built for enterprise ad analytics workflows with shared reports, role-based dashboards, automated email and Slack reporting, SOC 2-aligned security controls, encryption in transit and at rest, and custom integrations.
- Reported outcomes include 200+ creatives per month for Cloaked, under 48 hours per creative batch versus 10 days before, and 10% lower CAC.
- Tracks competitor ads across Meta and TikTok, with Google support planned, so teams can monitor competitor creative activity and campaign changes in near real time.
- Supports gap analysis between owned ads and competitor ads, helping teams compare creative themes, messaging angles, formats, and market positioning.
- Includes organized folders and creative archives so teams can save competitor ads, internal examples, and research for long-term reference.
- Can turn competitor-inspired concepts into brand-aligned creative drafts using the team’s guidelines.
- Trusted by public companies like Noom, Rocket Money and Ethos.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that mainly need market-wide ad spend estimates or large external ad archives.


## 2. MediaRadar


Best for: Cross-media competitive advertising intelligence.


MediaRadar is an ad intelligence platform for large teams that need external visibility into competitor advertising, media spend, creative activity, and category-level market movement. It helps enterprise brands and agencies monitor how advertisers are spending, what campaigns they are running, which messages are changing, and how category activity is shifting across digital and traditional media.


Key features:


- Tracks advertising activity across 30+ media channels, including social, display, online video, streaming TV/CTV, TV, print, radio, OOH, and other cross-media formats.
- Covers 5M brands, 35M+ ad and campaign assets, and $280B in media spend intelligence.
- Captures competitive creatives at scale, with searchable access to 35M+ campaign creatives for messaging, product launch, brand campaign, and competitive creative analysis.
- Supports competitive advertising intelligence, media spend intelligence, market intelligence, and benchmarking workflows for brands, agencies, publishers, and platforms.
- Provides configurable competitive ad reports, real-time ad alerts, benchmarking inputs, and executive-ready market intelligence.
- Used by enterprise teams including Instacart for advertising analysis across streaming TV, social, online video, and search.
- Helps teams monitor competitor campaigns, media mix, spending patterns, messaging shifts, category trends, and share-of-voice changes.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that mainly want to analyze and improve the performance of their own ad creatives.


## 3. Pathmatics by Sensor Tower


Best for: Competitor spend, share of voice, and channel strategy


Pathmatics by Sensor Tower is an enterprise ad intelligence platform for teams that need external visibility into competitor advertising, media spend, share of voice, creatives, audiences, and channel strategy. It helps enterprise brands, agencies, and publishers analyze how competitors advertise across digital, social, OTT/CTV, retail media, and linear TV channels.


Highlights:


- Monitors advertising activity across social, display, video, mobile, OTT/CTV, retail media, and linear TV.
- Tracks competitor ad spend estimates, impressions, share of voice, channel mix, audience targeting, and seasonal investment trends.
- Provides visibility into competitor activity across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X/Twitter, Reddit, OTT, YouTube, display, video, and other paid media channels.
- Captures competitor creatives, messaging, placements, flighting, spend estimates, and audience profiles for competitive creative and media analysis.
- Supports competitive benchmarking, category rankings, side-by-side competitor comparisons, and market analysis for media planning and competitive strategy.
- Uses observed ad activity, measurement methodology, and modeling to estimate competitor spend and impressions at scale.
- Supports exportable reporting and enterprise workflows for competitive analysis, media planning, and executive market updates.
- Trusted by 2,500+ enterprises worldwide.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that mainly need creative-level reporting on their own campaigns instead of external competitor and media-spend visibility.


## 4. AdClarity


Best for: Global ad intelligence and media spend benchmarking.


AdClarity is an ad intelligence tools for enterprises for brands and agencies that need to analyze competitor advertising across digital, social, CTV, mobile, and TV channels. It helps teams estimate competitor spend, track campaign activity, inspect creatives, compare media mix, and benchmark market movement across global regions.


Key features:


- Monitors advertising activity across display, video, social, mobile, CTV, linear TV, and other emerging digital ad environments.
- Covers display, video, and social campaigns across 650,000+ publishers and 50+ global markets.
- Tracks competitor ad spend estimates, impressions, publishers, audiences, media mix, campaigns, and share of voice.
- Captures competitor creatives, placements, publishers, and campaign activity for competitive creative analysis.
- Supports competitive insights, trend detection, custom dashboards, benchmarking, and exportable reports.
- Supports regional market analysis, competitive benchmarking, and media strategy analysis for brands, agencies, publishers, and research teams.
- Used by enterprises like Adidas, Amazon, Booking.com, Disney, Shell, Sony, and Wix.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that mainly need owned-campaign analytics rather than global competitive ad intelligence.


## 5. SocialPeta


Best for: Mobile app, gaming, and ecommerce ad intelligence.


SocialPeta is an enterprise ad intelligence platform for brands, agencies, mobile app marketers, gaming teams, and ecommerce teams that need to monitor competitor advertising, analyze creative trends, and compare competitor campaigns across global app, gaming, and ecommerce markets. It combines large-scale ad creative intelligence with AI-powered creative analysis and market research for international performance marketing.


Highlights:


- Monitors web, mobile apps, ecommerce, social platforms, and global ad networks across 80+ countries.
- Database of 1.7B+ ad creatives with daily updates covering millions of advertisers, apps, and campaigns.
- Tracks competitor creatives, advertising trends, channel activity, market saturation, and emerging campaigns through real-time competitive intelligence.
- AI analyzes assets to identify winning hooks, messaging, visual elements, selling points, storytelling patterns, and creative structures.
- Provides country trends, competitive benchmarking, channel comparisons, market opportunity analysis, and app/ecommerce revenue/download insights.
- Includes AI-powered workflow tools for creative analysis, ad research, translation, and strategy generation; used by Tencent, ByteDance, Alibaba Games, miHoYo, Baidu, and NetEase.


Limitation: Less suited for teams outside app, gaming, ecommerce, or performance marketing-heavy categories.


## 6. Adlyse


Best for: AI-powered paid media optimization intelligence.


Adlyse is an AI-powered enterprise ad intelligence platform for performance marketing teams that need to analyze campaign performance, detect wasted spend, surface optimization opportunities, and automate recurring paid media workflows. It connects campaign data across advertising platforms and uses AI agents to monitor performance, recommend actions, and support faster optimization decisions.


Key features:


- Connects advertising platforms, AI models, creative tools, and marketing data into a unified paid media intelligence layer.
- Continuously analyzes campaign performance, detects wasted spend, identifies pacing issues, and surfaces optimization opportunities.
- Uses AI agents to automate reporting, campaign monitoring, budget analysis, pacing checks, and recurring workflows.
- Learns from historical campaign performance to improve recommendations through a shared decision engine.
- Delivers proactive insights instead of static dashboards, surfacing issues, trends, and optimization opportunities as they emerge.
- Integrates into marketing workflows and communicates recommendations through collaboration channels; designed for large budgets across Google Ads, Meta, and related platforms.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that mainly want competitor ad research rather than campaign optimization intelligence.


## 7. AdSpy


Best for: Facebook and Instagram ad search.


AdSpy is a social ad intelligence platform for teams that need to search, monitor, and analyze Facebook and Instagram advertising at scale. It provides one of the world’s largest searchable databases of Meta ads, supporting competitive research, campaign inspiration, social ad analysis, and global advertising intelligence.


Highlights:


- Searchable database of 205M+ Facebook and Instagram ads from over 29M advertisers across 225 countries.
- Tracks competitor advertising, ad longevity, engagement, comments, demographics, landing pages, affiliate offers, and advertiser activity.
- Advanced search and filtering across ad copy, creatives, page names, URLs, offer IDs, media types, languages, and engagement metrics.
- Comment-based search to identify customer sentiment, competitor mentions, brand discussions, and high-performing campaigns.
- Provides demographic insights including estimated audience location, age, and gender targeting for competitive campaign analysis.
- Supports ecommerce brands, agencies, and performance marketers with global social advertising research.


Limitation: Less suited for teams that need broad enterprise ad intelligence beyond Facebook and Instagram ad search.


## How to Choose an Enterprise Ad Intelligence Platform


The right platform depends on whether your team needs first-party paid media analytics, creative-level intelligence, external competitor monitoring, or market-wide spend visibility. Evaluate channel coverage, creative data depth, competitor intelligence, and enterprise reporting requirements before choosing.


### 1. Paid Media Intelligence Coverage


Start with channel coverage (Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, programmatic, retail media, etc.). The platform should analyze performance at campaign, ad set, ad, and creative levels (spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, custom KPIs). For cross-channel teams, normalization is critical so you can compare performance across platforms with different naming, attribution windows, and reporting formats.


### 2. Creative Intelligence Depth


For creative-heavy teams, verify whether the platform can explain why ads perform. Look for creative-level analysis across video, image, copy, overlays, and landing pages, and for the ability to link those attributes to paid media performance to identify winning patterns and fatigue.


### 3. Competitive Advertising Intelligence


If you need external market visibility, prioritize platforms that monitor competitor ads, messaging trends, offers, campaign activity, media mix, and share-of-voice signals. This is especially valuable for benchmarking category movement, spotting launches, and tracking competitor positioning across channels and regions.


### 4. Enterprise Analytics Requirements


Evaluate permissions, data freshness, integrations, reporting workflows, and multi-brand/multi-market support. Some platforms focus on searchable competitor archives, while others connect to first-party ad accounts, attribution systems, BI tools, and data warehouses for internal reporting and optimization.
